what_happened.line: The Master Plan Steering Committee held a community workshop in which the consultant team presented existing-conditions findings; no votes or budget decisions were taken.
The findings covered demographics, housing growth, land use, zoning and sewer, public facilities, economic development, transportation, and history and open space.
Residents met in breakout groups on what they value and would change; spokespeople reported wants such as affordable housing for elderly and young people, walkability and sidewalks.
One group asked the town to set aside money to maintain facilities such as school and public safety building roofs.
A committee member urged residents to watch recorded meetings on YouTube and follow the master plan Facebook page and website.

why_it_matters: The master plan sets the town's long-range direction on housing, land use, sidewalks and facilities upkeep, and resident input at this stage shapes what later zoning and capital proposals are built on.
Nothing here changes a tax bill or a service yet; the facilities-maintenance set-aside is a suggestion from one group, not a proposal.
